name: shellbags
description: Walk BagMRU in UsrClass.dat or NTUSER.DAT and return the folders a shell opened on this account: the reconstructed path, the key's last-write time (raw FILETIME and ISO), the shell item's own DOS timestamps (local time, to two seconds) and the MRU order. It reaches folders on devices and shares that are long gone; it does not say who opened them. Every BagMRU root the hive has is walked and named (the Shell and ShellNoRoam trees can both be populated) and each entry says which; a numbered value with no key under it is decoded and listed under values_without_subkey, not dropped; values are read whole (regipy's default cut to 128 bytes is not taken). A shell item's long name is read from its layout only for the file entry extension (0xbeef0004) versions 3, 7, 8 and 9, at the offset the libfwsi notes give for the version (0x14, 0x26, 0x2A, 0x2E), bounded by the block's declared size, and only when the block's own name offset (the 2-byte field at 0x10) agrees and what is there is a printable string that ends inside the block (long_name_from: layout, extension_layout: decoded; a localised name after it, where there is one, is localized_name); in any other case the long name is the longest string found in the block, labelled long_name_from: strings with extension_layout saying why the layout was not applied, a candidate and not a decode. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive: a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values, so an index that repeats one list (an ri element named again and again) is read to that bound, listed once per key, and said under problems; it is not followed. A key whose subkey list was already walked (a cycle) is a problem, not walked again; a shell item that cannot be decoded is listed as undecodable. Other shell item classes are string candidates (decoded: strings). max_depth is 1 to 128; keys below it are listed under not_walked_below_max_depth, and problems are a page. The tool stops at its own time limit (114 seconds) and names the keys it did not walk (status partial); past it the first 1,000 further keys and entries are named and listed and the rest are only counted (not_walked_not_named, entries_not_listed_for_time), not judged; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. Result files are named from the hive, the roots and whether contains was given, never from the needle, and are never replaced (another needle takes the next free -n name). The library's own messages, which can hold bytes of a name, are counted and never printed. Every answer carries status and status_basis. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (shell item names, paths and registry keys): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (SEAL_BUDGET, 10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool, which is 3.5 seconds before its time limit because the string being judged at that point is finished first and one string of 256 KiB can take up to 2.3 seconds) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole by <withheld N bytes: backstop: the judging time ran out>, counted and listed, and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself (its keys, the names of its result files, the name of the hive, its status basis) and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token and, in a field of a typed kind (a SID, a GUID, a digest), fits the grammar of its type (so not a Slack-shaped token, not the value after a flag such as -pwd, not a prefix and 12 characters). The seal stop ends the judging only, not the tool's own work, which has its own, earlier clock. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). A filter on content (contains) is applied to the text the answer prints (after the layers and the backstop), never to what either withheld or replaced: what it did not match and has text withheld in it is counted (contains_blind_entries) and makes the answer partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld; the count is the same whatever the needle is. ORDER: the entries are walked in the order of the text shown for each BagMRU slot name (withheld names in an order of their own that is new for every run), and the names listed when a key is not found likewise, not in the order the hive stores them (alphabetical by raw name): what a listing is ordered by is only what the answer shows. write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: about 0.1% printed whole (0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 plants of the block's own harness; 1 of 105 canaries end to end, the same canary in four slots; an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940), so the rate is small and not zero. The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). The average hides channels: PowerShell/Operational has the XML of 25.0% of its 1,857 records replaced whole (script blocks carry base64 and long identifiers) and CodeIntegrity/Operational 33.3% of its 1,309 (event 3089, whose Hash is a padded base64 digest). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. DIRTY HIVE: hive_dirty (the two sequence numbers differ), the log files looked for (transaction_logs_looked_for: the hive's name with .LOG1, .LOG2 and .LOG) and the ones beside the hive (transaction_logs_beside_hive) are reported; the logs are NOT replayed, so every answer from a dirty hive is partial and status_basis names the caveat (what is read is the hive file as it is, and keys and values may differ from the live registry; registry_recover replays the logs on a copy, which this tool then reads). A log that is not among the files the job can read is not found: declare the hive's .LOG1 and .LOG2 as inputs of the job. INLINE VALUES: a value whose data is inside its record (four bytes at most) is read from the record for every registry type. regipy 6.3.0 reads up to 2 GiB of the hive file for such a value and returns that for a type it has no branch for (a device property under a Properties key, REG_LINK, REG_FILETIME, an unknown type), so one such value came back as megabytes of the hive; this tool replaces that read. BIG DATA AND REG_MULTI_SZ: the values of a key are read by this tool from regipy's copy of the hive, with regipy 6.3.0's records, names, types and decoding, and a value of more than 16,344 bytes that is kept in segments (a db record) is checked before its data is put together: one that declares more data than the hive file holds past its base block, whose list holds fewer segments than its size needs, runs past the end of the file or names one segment more than once, or one of whose segments lies past the end of the file, is not read; it is named under problems by its place in the key's value list and its type, and the answer is partial (regipy put together whatever the list named: one 16 KB segment named 160 times was a 2.5 MiB value, and a 548 KB hive declared one of 2 GiB). Every value's data counts against the walk's data budget (four times the hive's size) before it is read. A value that declares more than 16 MiB of data is not read: it is named under problems with the length it declares. The values of a key are handed out one at a time and stop at 64 MiB of data for the key, said under problems. A subkey list keeps each key the first time it names it, and is read no further after 4,096 elements in a row that name keys it already named, or past about 190,000 distinct keys (256 MiB of memory), each said under problems; a subkey list begun after the time limit is read to 16,384 elements and a value list to 4,096, and what is left is said. The hive is opened only when its base block and first bin are what regipy's open reads (the regf signature, a first bin of a positive multiple of 4096 bytes, the root cell the base block names inside the bins, allocated and a key, and the first allocated cell of the first bin that same cell): any other file is a failure that says what was found (regipy read a first bin of free space four bytes at a time, with no clock: a 40 MB hive took 58 s). MRUListEx is read for at most as many entries as the key has values and subkeys. A later value of a name the key already holds (names are matched without regard to case) is listed as a value without a subkey and said under problems. The status basis counts the keys not walked for the time limit apart from the keys below max_depth. A REG_MULTI_SZ is split by this tool in one pass and gives the strings regipy gives (empty ones left out); the bytes after its last NUL, and a string that is not valid UTF-16 with the rest of the data after it, are not in the answer, as with regipy, and are said under problems with their length (regipy dropped them without a word, and took 50 s on 2 MiB with no NUL). The tool's deadline is read before every value and every 256 subkey elements of a list begun before it: the values or subkeys of a key that were not read in time are said under problems. The BagMRU roots are looked up through the same bounded subkey lists (regipy's get_key read an index on the way as many times as it repeats a list).

hive.description: An extracted UsrClass.dat (or NTUSER.DAT for the older location)

key.description: Override the BagMRU root when the hive puts it somewhere unusual (then only that root is walked)

contains.description: Keep only paths containing this string, case-insensitive; the text is looked at as shown, so a needle inside withheld text matches nothing and what it did not match but has text withheld is counted and makes the answer partial

max_depth.description: How deep to walk (default 24, at most 128); a key below it that has subkeys is named in not_walked_below_max_depth

limit.description: Entries shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole tree is walked, and when more entries match the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
